usage: This is the standard, universally understood phrase for welcoming someone to a place, such as a home, office, or country. It is appropriate for all levels of formality in Cairo. In everyday conversation, it is very frequently adapted to include a pronoun suffix, such as 'ahlan biik', to directly address the person.

variants.label: to a man
variants.note: The most common way to welcome a single male.

variants.label: to a woman
variants.note: The most common way to welcome a single female.

variants.label: to a group
variants.note: Used when welcoming two or more people.

variants.label: enthusiastic
variants.note: Used to show extreme warmth and hospitality to a guest.

responses.english: Welcome to you too (to a man)
Welcome to you too (to a woman)

examples.arabic: يَا مِيت أَهْلاً وَسَهْلاً، نَوَّرْتُوا البِيت!
examples.transliteration: ya miit ahlan wa sahlan, nawwartu el beit!
examples.english: A hundred welcomes, you have lit up the house!
